newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond and interest rate futures came under pressure as an opinion poll suggesting the ruling coalition would win only a slim majority unsettled an already nervous marketplace.

The June bond future, which had climbed earlier with Bunds, slipped from a high of 128.94 to settle at 128.62 and continued to fall on GLOBEX, touching a low of 128.40. June PIBOR tumbled 10 basis points from its earlier high and fell more on GLOBEX.
Traders said the rot had set in after an earlier poll which showed 69 percent of the French wanted another referendum on European monetary union.
The French franc fell as low as 3.3753 per mark from an earlier high of 3.3690, its strongest level since last Friday.
"Clearly after the bounce on Monday and Tuesday people were starting to feel confident the right was gong to get in," a bond analyst at a French bank said.
He said an IPSOS poll, which gave the ruling coalition 292 seats, "has put the market back on edge. We're back to where were last Friday when speculation was at its highest."
Marie Owens Thomsen at Louis Dreyfus said, "I realise that the market will be worried about polls like this one that show (the election) will be a close one."
"I still live in the world where I believe the Socialists are not organized enough to present a credible alternative," Owens Thomsen said.

"Basically I'm not worried, perhaps being naive I still believe the conservatives will win and if I have a worry it's not a Socialist win it's the extreme parties getting enough votes to take on a pivotal role," she said.
An opinion poll, conducted on April 7 and 8, on President Jacques Chirac's popularity, will be released overnight.
